key_insight: A message-passing reinforcement learning architecture coordinates global and node-level network control while preserving permutation symmetries and transparency constraints.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports scalable decisions that combine network-wide resource budgets with institution-specific allocations in systemic-risk management.
method: Use message passing with separate global and local policy heads.
Derive explicit Lipschitz bounds for parameter and input perturbations.
Use these bounds to establish projected policy-gradient convergence guarantees.
evidence_signal: Financial-network experiments report better performance than feedforward-network baselines and scalability to large networks, but the abstract provides no numerical metrics or network sizes.
watch_item: Sensitivity and convergence depend on architectural choices and graph characteristics, so robustness should be checked on the intended deployment networks.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning for Global-Local Control of Dynamic Networks with Applications to Systemic Risk
